```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# toxval 2.0.0, the main branch of open-AIMS/toxval. In the package this line
# is library(toxval).
source("../../R/toxval_at.R")
toxval_sha <- attr(toxval_at("016402dad441ad9c76c5dc9704b16cbd3c19c2d5"), "sha")
# formatting for inline numbers, so that every value in the prose is computed
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f", big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(x, digits = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, digits = digits, format = "f"), "%")
```

```{r}
#| label: packages
library(ggplot2)
```

The `drc` package fits concentration-response curves with `drm()`, and
estimates effect concentrations from a fitted curve with `ED()`. toxval's
`ecx()` and `nsec()` also accept a `drm()` fit, so a fitted curve can be
summarised with either package. Here we fit two datasets shipped with `drc` and
compare the estimates from each package: `ryegrass`, a continuous response
described by one curve, and `daphnids`, a binomial response described by one
curve for each of two exposure times. The definitions used by toxval are given
in the articles on the [ECx](https://open-aims.github.io/toxval/articles/ecx-definition.html)
and the [NSEC](https://open-aims.github.io/toxval/articles/nsec-definition.html).

## A single curve

```{r}
#| label: ryegrass-data
#| include: false
ryegrass <- drc::ryegrass
n_conc <- length(unique(ryegrass$conc[ryegrass$conc > 0]))
n_control <- sum(ryegrass$conc == 0)
```

`ryegrass` contains the root length (cm) of perennial ryegrass grown at
`r n_conc` concentrations of ferulic acid, from `r min(ryegrass$conc[ryegrass$conc > 0])`
to `r max(ryegrass$conc)` mM, and in `r n_control` controls without it. We
fitted the four-parameter log-logistic equation `LL.4()`, in which the response
declines from an upper limit `d` to a lower limit `c`, with a slope `b` and with
`e` the concentration at which the response is halfway between `d` and `c`.

```{r}
#| label: fit-ryegrass
fit <- drc::drm(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, fct = drc::LL.4())
summary(fit)
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-values
#| include: false
p <- coef(fit)
names(p) <- sub(":.*", "", names(p))
```

The fitted root length declines from `r fmt(p[["d"]])` cm to
`r fmt(p[["c"]])` cm, and is halfway between these limits at
`r fmt(p[["e"]])` mM.

### The confidence band on the curve

Both packages give a 95% confidence band on the fitted curve, although they
compute it differently. In `drc`, `predict()` with `interval = "confidence"`
gives a band from the delta method (a linear approximation of the curve at the
parameter estimates). toxval's `toxval_predict()` instead draws `n_boot`
parameter vectors (1000 by default) from a multivariate normal distribution
with mean `coef(fit)` and covariance `vcov(fit)`, and evaluates the curve at
each vector. A parameter that the equation requires to be positive (here `e`)
is drawn on the log scale. We refer to each evaluated curve as a realisation
(i.e. a parametric bootstrap replicate), and took the band as the 2.5 and 97.5
percentiles of the realisations at each concentration. By default the
realisations are evaluated at 500 concentrations from the control
concentration (here 0 mM) to the highest concentration in the data, and we
evaluated the `drc` band at these concentrations. `ecx()` and `nsec()` call
`toxval_predict()` themselves, and the `seed` argument of each function makes
the realisations reproducible.

```{r}
#| label: bands-ryegrass
#| warning: false
pred <- toxval_predict(fit, seed = 42)
toxval_q <- apply(pred$curves[[1]], 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
bands <- data.frame(
  conc = pred$x_vec,
  predict(fit, data.frame(conc = pred$x_vec), interval = "confidence"),
  toxval_lower = toxval_q[1, ],
  toxval_upper = toxval_q[2, ]
)
head(bands)
```

```{r}
#| label: bands-ryegrass-values
#| include: false
gap_low <- bands$toxval_lower - bands$Lower
gap_high <- bands$toxval_upper - bands$Upper
band_gap <- pmax(abs(gap_low), abs(gap_high))
at_gap <- which.max(band_gap)
stopifnot(
  max(band_gap) < 0.25,
  gap_low[at_gap] < 0,
  gap_high[at_gap] < 0
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bands-ryegrass
#| fig-cap: "Root length of ryegrass against the concentration of ferulic acid (points), with the `LL.4()` fit (black line), the 95% confidence band from `predict()` in `drc` (grey) and the 95% band from the toxval realisations (dashed blue lines). The concentration axis is a pseudo-logarithmic scale, which is linear near 0 and logarithmic above about 0.1 mM, so that the controls can be shown."
#| fig-height: 4
p_ryegrass <- ggplot(bands, aes(conc)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper, fill = "drc"), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = toxval_lower, colour = "toxval"), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = toxval_upper, colour = "toxval"), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Prediction)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = rootl), data = ryegrass) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    transform = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.1),
    breaks = c(0, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30),
    labels = c("0", "0.3", "1", "3", "10", "30")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(drc = "grey50")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(toxval = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(x = "Ferulic acid (mM)", y = "Root length (cm)", fill = "95% band", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
p_ryegrass
```

The `drc` and toxval bands are close over the observed range
(@fig-bands-ryegrass), and their limits differ by at most
`r fmt(max(band_gap))` cm. The largest difference is at
`r fmt(bands$conc[at_gap])` mM, at the start of the decline, where both limits
of the toxval band are below those of the `drc` band.

### EC10 and EC50

`ED()` and `ecx()` measure the effect from different points by default, so we
matched their definitions before comparing the estimates. Both packages express
the effect as a proportion of the difference between two response values.
`ED()` uses the fitted limits `d` and `c`, so its EC10 is the concentration at
which the response has fallen by 10% of `d - c`. `ecx()` takes the effect as a
proportion (e.g. `proportion = 0.1` for the EC10), always starts from the
control (the predicted response at the lowest concentration in the data, here
0 mM), and takes the other value from its `type` argument. Under
`type = "relative"` the other value is `c`, and because `LL.4()` equals `d` at
a concentration of 0, this matches the definition used by `ED()`. Under the
default, `type = "absolute"`, the other value is 0, so the EC10 is the
concentration at which the response is 90% of the control.

```{r}
#| label: ed-ryegrass
ed <- drc::ED(fit, c(10, 50), interval = "delta")
```

```{r}
#| label: ecx-relative
#| warning: false
ecx_rel <- ecx(fit, proportion = c(0.1, 0.5), type = "relative", seed = 42)
ecx_rel
```

```{r}
#| label: ecx-absolute
ecx_abs <- ecx(fit, proportion = c(0.1, 0.5), seed = 42)
ecx_abs
```

`ecx()` returns a row for each direction of change. Because this curve only
declines, the increasing rows are `NA`. The `reference` column gives the
response at which each ECx is read, and the `control` column the response it is
measured from.

```{r}
#| label: ec-ryegrass
from_ecx <- function(res, method) {
  dec <- res[res$direction == "decreasing", ]
  data.frame(
    method,
    effect = paste0("EC", 100 * dec$proportion),
    estimate = dec$estimate,
    lower = dec$conf.low,
    upper = dec$conf.high
  )
}
ec_ryegrass <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    method = "ED()",
    effect = c("EC10", "EC50"),
    estimate = ed[, "Estimate"],
    lower = ed[, "Lower"],
    upper = ed[, "Upper"],
    row.names = NULL
  ),
  from_ecx(ecx_rel, "ecx(), relative"),
  from_ecx(ecx_abs, "ecx(), absolute")
)
ec_ryegrass
```

```{r}
#| label: ec-ryegrass-values
#| include: false
ec <- function(tab, method, effect) tab[tab$method == method & tab$effect == effect, ]
ed10 <- ec(ec_ryegrass, "ED()", "EC10")
ed50 <- ec(ec_ryegrass, "ED()", "EC50")
rel10 <- ec(ec_ryegrass, "ecx(), relative", "EC10")
rel50 <- ec(ec_ryegrass, "ecx(), relative", "EC50")
abs10 <- ec(ec_ryegrass, "ecx(), absolute", "EC10")
abs50 <- ec(ec_ryegrass, "ecx(), absolute", "EC50")
ref_rel <- ecx_rel$reference[ecx_rel$direction == "decreasing"][1]
ref_abs <- ecx_abs$reference[ecx_abs$direction == "decreasing"][1]
rel_gap <- max(abs(c(rel10$estimate / ed10$estimate, rel50$estimate / ed50$estimate) - 1))
stopifnot(
  all(is.na(ecx_rel$estimate[ecx_rel$direction == "increasing"])),
  all(is.na(ecx_abs$estimate[ecx_abs$direction == "increasing"])),
  ref_abs < ref_rel,
  abs10$estimate > rel10$estimate,
  abs50$estimate > rel50$estimate,
  rel_gap < 0.02
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ec-ryegrass
#| fig-cap: "The EC10 (left) and EC50 (right) of the `LL.4()` fit to `ryegrass` from `ED()` and from `ecx()` under two definitions. Points: the estimates. Lines: the 95% intervals, from the delta method for `ED()` and from the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of 1000 realisations for `ecx()`."
#| fig-height: 2.6
ggplot(ec_ryegrass, aes(estimate, method)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper)) +
  facet_wrap(~effect, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(unique(ec_ryegrass$method))) +
  labs(x = "Ferulic acid (mM)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Under the matched definition, the two packages return very similar results:
`ecx()` gives an EC10 of `r fmt(rel10$estimate)` mM and an EC50 of
`r fmt(rel50$estimate)` mM, compared with `r fmt(ed10$estimate)` and
`r fmt(ed50$estimate)` mM from `ED()` (@fig-ec-ryegrass). The default `ecx()`
estimates are higher (`r fmt(abs10$estimate)` and `r fmt(abs50$estimate)` mM),
because its EC10 is read at a lower response (`r fmt(ref_abs)` cm, compared with
`r fmt(ref_rel)` cm under `relative`). These reference responses differ by a
tenth of the lower limit `c`, so the difference between the `absolute` and
`relative` estimates would be larger for a curve with a higher lower limit. For
these data `c` is small compared with `d` (`r fmt(p[["c"]])` against
`r fmt(p[["d"]])` cm), and the `absolute` and `relative` intervals overlap for
both estimates.

```{r}
#| label: interval-values
#| include: false
t_mult <- qt(0.975, df.residual(fit))
side <- function(row) c(below = row$estimate - row$lower, above = row$upper - row$estimate)
ed10_side <- side(ed10)
rel10_side <- side(rel10)
stopifnot(
  abs(ed10_side[["below"]] / ed[1, "Std. Error"] - t_mult) < 1e-6,
  abs(ed10_side[["below"]] - ed10_side[["above"]]) < 1e-8,
  rel10_side[["below"]] > rel10_side[["above"]],
  rel10$lower < ed10$lower,
  rel10$upper < ed10$upper
)
```

The intervals differ because the packages convert the uncertainty in the
parameters into an interval on the ECx in different ways, although both take
that uncertainty from `vcov(fit)`. The delta method used by `ED()` replaces the
ECx by its linear approximation at the parameter estimates. This gives a
standard error, and an interval of the estimate plus or minus
`r fmt(t_mult)` standard errors (the 0.975 quantile of a *t* distribution on
`r df.residual(fit)` residual degrees of freedom), which is symmetric by
construction. `ecx()` instead finds the ECx of each realisation and returns the
median and the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of these values. Its interval can
therefore be asymmetric where the ECx is a nonlinear function of the
parameters. For example, the `relative` EC10 interval extends
`r fmt(rel10_side[["below"]])` mM below the estimate and
`r fmt(rel10_side[["above"]])` mM above it, whereas the `ED()` interval extends
`r fmt(ed10_side[["below"]])` mM on each side. The point estimates also differ
slightly, because `ED()` gives the ECx at the parameter estimates whereas
`ecx()` gives the median over the realisations.

The `ecx()` limits are percentiles of a finite set of realisations, so they
change slightly with the `seed`. A larger `n_boot` reduces this variation,
although the computation then takes longer.

## NSEC

The no-significant-effect concentration (NSEC) is the concentration at which the
fitted response departs from the control by more than the uncertainty in the
control allows. `drc` does not provide a method for estimating the NSEC from a
fitted model, and this is one of the motivations for the development of toxval.
`nsec()` takes as its reference the 0.01 quantile (set by `sig_val`) of the
control across the realisations, finds the concentration at which each
realisation crosses that reference, and summarises these concentrations as for
`ecx()`.

```{r}
#| label: nsec-ryegrass
ns <- nsec(fit, seed = 42)
ns
ns_dec <- ns[ns$direction == "decreasing", ]
```

```{r}
#| label: nsec-values
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  is.na(ns$estimate[ns$direction == "increasing"]),
  ns_dec$estimate < rel10$estimate,
  ns_dec$reference < ns_dec$control
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-nsec-ryegrass
#| fig-cap: "@fig-bands-ryegrass with the decreasing NSEC from `nsec()` (vermillion line) and its 95% interval (vermillion shading), and the reference response used by `nsec()` (dotted line)."
#| fig-height: 4
p_ryegrass +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = ns_dec$conf.low, xmax = ns_dec$conf.high, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ns_dec$estimate, colour = "#D55E00") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ns_dec$reference, linetype = 3)
```

The NSEC is `r fmt(ns_dec$estimate)` mM (`r fmt(ns_dec$conf.low)` to
`r fmt(ns_dec$conf.high)`), the concentration at which the curve falls below the
reference of `r fmt(ns_dec$reference)` cm (@fig-nsec-ryegrass). This is below
the EC10 of `r fmt(rel10$estimate)` mM, and the `ecnsec` column gives the effect
at the NSEC as a proportion of the control, here `r pct(ns_dec$ecnsec, 1)`.

`drc` also provides equations with a threshold (e.g. `NEC.3()`), in which the
response is constant up to a no-effect concentration (NEC) that is estimated as
the parameter `e`. `nsec()` does not accept fits of these equations.

## A grouped fit

`daphnids` contains the number of immobile daphnids out of 20 at
`r length(unique(drc::daphnids$dose))` concentrations of a toxic substance, from
`r min(drc::daphnids$dose)` to `r fmt(max(drc::daphnids$dose), 0)`, counted
after 24 h and again (in the same animals) after 48 h. Because the response is a
count out of a known total, we fitted the two-parameter log-logistic equation
`LL.2()` with `type = "binomial"` and the total as weights, with one curve per
exposure time (`curveid = time`). `LL.2()` fixes the lower limit at 0 and the
upper limit at 1, so the fitted response is the proportion immobile.

```{r}
#| label: fit-daphnids
daphnids <- drc::daphnids
fit_daph <- drc::drm(
  no / total ~ dose,
  weights = total,
  curveid = time,
  data = daphnids,
  fct = drc::LL.2(),
  type = "binomial"
)
ed_daph <- drc::ED(fit_daph, c(10, 50), interval = "delta")
```

In `ecx()`, the column passed to `drm()` as `curveid` is given in `group_var`,
and the result has one set of rows per curve, identified by the `group` column.

```{r}
#| label: ecx-daphnids
ecx_daph <- ecx(fit_daph, proportion = c(0.1, 0.5), group_var = "time", seed = 42)
ecx_daph
```

```{r}
#| label: ecx-daphnids-relative
#| include: false
ecx_daph_rel <- suppressWarnings(
  ecx(fit_daph, proportion = c(0.1, 0.5), group_var = "time", type = "relative", seed = 42)
)
stopifnot(
  identical(ecx_daph_rel$estimate, ecx_daph$estimate),
  identical(ecx_daph_rel$conf.low, ecx_daph$conf.low),
  identical(ecx_daph_rel$conf.high, ecx_daph$conf.high),
  all(ecx_daph_rel$asymptote[ecx_daph_rel$direction == "increasing"] == 1)
)
```

Because the proportion immobile rises with concentration, the estimates are in
the increasing rows. `ED()` takes the increasing effect as a proportion of the
difference between `c` and `d`, which `LL.2()` fixes at 0 and 1. Unlike the
`ryegrass` fit, this fit does not need `type = "relative"` for `ecx()` and
`ED()` to agree. For `ryegrass` the packages differed in the value the response
falls towards (0 for the default `ecx()` and `c` for `ED()`), and
`type = "relative"` replaced 0 by `c`. Here, for a response on the proportion
scale, the default `type = "absolute"` already takes the value the response
rises towards as 1, which is also the upper limit `d` of `LL.2()`, so
`type = "relative"` returns identical estimates and intervals. The packages
differ instead in the value the response rises from. `ecx()` starts from the
control, the predicted proportion immobile at the lowest tested concentration
(`r min(daphnids$dose)`), which is `r fmt(ecx_daph$control[2], 4)` at 24 h and
`r fmt(ecx_daph$control[6], 4)` at 48 h, whereas `ED()` starts from `c` = 0.
The `type` argument does not change the control, but `x_control` does:
supplying `x_control = 0` predicts the control at a concentration of 0, where
`LL.2()` equals 0, and the definitions then coincide.

```{r}
#| label: ecx-daphnids-zero
ecx_daph0 <- ecx(
  fit_daph,
  proportion = c(0.1, 0.5),
  group_var = "time",
  x_control = 0,
  seed = 42
)
```

The call gives two warnings. The first is that 0 is outside the tested
concentrations, so the control is a prediction beyond the data. The second is
that the decreasing rows have no reference, because a proportion cannot fall
below a control of 0.

```{r}
#| label: ec-daphnids
from_ecx_group <- function(res, method) {
  inc <- res[res$direction == "increasing", ]
  data.frame(
    time = inc$group,
    method,
    effect = paste0("EC", 100 * inc$proportion),
    estimate = inc$estimate,
    lower = inc$conf.low,
    upper = inc$conf.high
  )
}
ec_daph <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    time = sub("e:(.*):.*", "\\1", rownames(ed_daph)),
    method = "ED()",
    effect = paste0("EC", sub(".*:", "", rownames(ed_daph))),
    estimate = ed_daph[, "Estimate"],
    lower = ed_daph[, "Lower"],
    upper = ed_daph[, "Upper"],
    row.names = NULL
  ),
  from_ecx_group(ecx_daph, "ecx()"),
  from_ecx_group(ecx_daph0, "ecx(), x_control = 0")
)
ec_daph <- ec_daph[order(ec_daph$time, ec_daph$effect), ]
ec_daph
```

```{r}
#| label: ec-daphnids-values
#| include: false
gap <- function(method, effect) {
  ed_rows <- ec_daph[ec_daph$method == "ED()" & ec_daph$effect == effect, ]
  tx_rows <- ec_daph[ec_daph$method == method & ec_daph$effect == effect, ]
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(ed_rows$time), as.character(tx_rows$time)))
  max(abs(tx_rows$estimate / ed_rows$estimate - 1))
}
gap0 <- c(EC10 = gap("ecx(), x_control = 0", "EC10"), EC50 = gap("ecx(), x_control = 0", "EC50"))
gap_default <- c(EC10 = gap("ecx()", "EC10"), EC50 = gap("ecx()", "EC50"))
row_of <- function(time, method, effect) {
  ec_daph[ec_daph$time == time & ec_daph$method == method & ec_daph$effect == effect, ]
}
ed50_24 <- row_of("24h", "ED()", "EC50")
tx50_24 <- row_of("24h", "ecx(), x_control = 0", "EC50")
stopifnot(
  identical(as.character(ecx_daph$group[c(2, 6)]), c("24h", "48h")),
  all(is.na(ecx_daph$estimate[ecx_daph$direction == "decreasing"])),
  gap0[["EC50"]] < 0.01,
  gap0[["EC10"]] < gap_default[["EC10"]],
  tx50_24$upper > ed50_24$upper,
  tx50_24$upper - tx50_24$estimate > tx50_24$estimate - tx50_24$lower,
  abs((ed50_24$upper - ed50_24$estimate) - (ed50_24$estimate - ed50_24$lower)) < 1e-6
)
```

```{r}
#| label: bands-daphnids
#| warning: false
pred_daph <- toxval_predict(fit_daph, group_var = "time", seed = 42)
bands_daph <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(pred_daph$curves), function(i) {
  time <- as.character(pred_daph$keys$group[i])
  q <- apply(pred_daph$curves[[i]], 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
  data.frame(
    dose = pred_daph$x_vec,
    time,
    predict(fit_daph, data.frame(dose = pred_daph$x_vec, time = time), interval = "confidence"),
    toxval_lower = q[1, ],
    toxval_upper = q[2, ]
  )
}))
```

```{r}
#| label: bands-daphnids-values
#| include: false
at_low <- bands_daph[bands_daph$dose == min(daphnids$dose), ]
upper_at_low <- setNames(
  lapply(split(at_low, at_low$time), function(r) c(drc = r$Upper, toxval = r$toxval_upper)),
  sort(unique(at_low$time))
)
stopifnot(
  nrow(at_low) == 2,
  upper_at_low[["24h"]][["toxval"]] > upper_at_low[["24h"]][["drc"]],
  upper_at_low[["48h"]][["toxval"]] > upper_at_low[["48h"]][["drc"]]
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bands-daphnids
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of daphnids immobile against concentration at 24 h (left) and 48 h (right) (points), with the `LL.2()` fit (black line), the 95% confidence band from `predict()` in `drc` (grey) and the 95% band from the toxval realisations (dashed blue lines). The concentration axis is logarithmic."
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(bands_daph, aes(dose)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper, fill = "drc"), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = toxval_lower, colour = "toxval"), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = toxval_upper, colour = "toxval"), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Prediction)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = no / total), data = daphnids) +
  facet_wrap(~time) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(100, 300, 1000, 3000), labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(drc = "grey50")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(toxval = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(x = "Concentration", y = "Proportion immobile", fill = "95% band", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The `drc` and toxval bands are close in the steep part of each curve
(@fig-bands-daphnids). However, at the lowest concentration the upper limit of
the toxval band is higher, at `r fmt(upper_at_low[["24h"]][["toxval"]], 3)`
compared with `r fmt(upper_at_low[["24h"]][["drc"]], 3)` at 24 h. This appears
to be because the delta-method band is symmetric about the curve, whereas the
realisations are bounded below by 0 and skewed upwards where the fitted
proportion is near 0.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ec-daphnids
#| fig-cap: "The EC10 and EC50 of the `LL.2()` fits to `daphnids` at 24 h (top) and 48 h (bottom), from `ED()` and from `ecx()` with the control at the lowest tested concentration and at 0. Points: the estimates. Lines: the 95% intervals, from the delta method for `ED()` and from the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of 1000 realisations for `ecx()`."
#| fig-height: 4.2
ggplot(ec_daph, aes(estimate, method)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper)) +
  facet_wrap(~ time + effect, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2, labeller = label_wrap_gen(multi_line = FALSE)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(unique(ec_daph$method))) +
  labs(x = "Concentration", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

With the control at 0, the `ecx()` EC50s are within
`r pct(gap0[["EC50"]], 1)` of the `ED()` values and the EC10s within
`r pct(gap0[["EC10"]], 1)` (@fig-ec-daphnids). The remaining difference is
likely to come from the point estimate, which for `ecx()` is the median of the
realisations. With the control at the lowest tested concentration, the EC10s
differ from `ED()` by up to `r pct(gap_default[["EC10"]], 1)`, because the small
proportion immobile at that concentration raises the response at which the EC10
is read. The intervals differ in shape as for `ryegrass`. For example, the 24 h
EC50 interval from `ecx()` with the control at 0 runs from
`r fmt(tx50_24$lower, 0)` to `r fmt(tx50_24$upper, 0)`, and extends further
above the estimate than below it, whereas the delta-method interval from `ED()`
runs from `r fmt(ed50_24$lower, 0)` to `r fmt(ed50_24$upper, 0)` and is
symmetric.

## Provenance

```{r}
#| label: provenance
#| comment: ""
cat(sprintf("%-10s %s\n", "toxval", as.character(packageVersion("toxval"))))
cat(sprintf("%-10s %s\n", "commit", toxval_sha))
for (pkg in c("drc", "ggplot2")) {
  cat(sprintf("%-10s %s\n", pkg, as.character(packageVersion(pkg))))
}
cat(sprintf("%-10s %s\n", "R", getRversion()))
```

- Data: `ryegrass` and `daphnids` from the `drc` package, used as shipped.
- Fits: `drm()` with its default starting values.
- Realisations: `n_boot = 1000` parametric bootstrap draws with `seed = 42`.
- Grid: toxval's default of 500 evenly spaced concentrations from the control
  concentration to the highest concentration in the data.
- The commit line is the toxval commit loaded by `toxval_at()`.
